notes.thesis: The Financial Action Task Force is best classified as a global soft-law, peer-review, and listing waist for anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, and counter-proliferation-financing governance: its Recommendations, mutual evaluations, follow-up processes, and high-risk / increased-monitoring lists can harden through domestic law, supervisors, banks, correspondent relationships, procurement, insurance, and investor behavior, but they are not themselves a general world financial police power.

notes.title: 863 — Applied Schengen Information System alert-database waist: national issuer responsibility, data rights, and no European police by alert
notes.thesis: The Schengen Information System is best classified as a cross-border alert-database and operational-cooperation waist: it lets authorised national and EU-linked authorities enter, search, and act on alerts for defined persons and objects across Schengen cooperation, but each alert still needs legal category, issuing-authority responsibility, data-quality discipline, SIRENE / supplementary-information routing, access controls, correction / erasure rights, and national or EU legal bases, so the database must not become European police government by alert.

notes.title: 864 — Plural-order authority and Indigenous co-governance: legal personality, consent, settlement mandate, relational jurisdiction, and no sovereignty by consultation theater
notes.thesis: Plural-order authority should not be flattened into ordinary decentralization, consultation, or stakeholder management; when Indigenous law, treaty redress, legal personality, relational territory, and state public law meet, the archive must name each authority lane, consent threshold, record duty, operational owner, and remedy route before it calls the arrangement legitimate.

notes.title: 865 — Applied plural-order case packet for Taranaki Maunga / Te Kāhui Tupua: legal-person mountain, iwi-Crown conservation waist, and no park government by ownership fiction
notes.thesis: The Taranaki Maunga / Te Kāhui Tupua settlement is best treated as a plural-order legal-person natural-entity and conservation-governance waist: it recognises an ancestral mountain as a legal person and creates iwi-Crown voice, plan, approval, and monitoring routes, but it should not be described either as ordinary national-park consultation or as a fully separate territorial government.

notes.title: 866 — Applied supplier-dependency case packet for NHS Federated Data Platform: Palantir-led SaaS, PET, instances, exit proof, and no health service by data console
notes.thesis: The NHS Federated Data Platform is best treated as a supplier-dependent operational data-platform waist: a federated SaaS service used by NHS England, trusts, and integrated care boards to connect operational health data, where public control, local controller duties, privacy-enhancing technology, audit logs, product boundaries, migration rights, staff trust, patient rights, and exit proof must be visible before the platform is praised as transformation or condemned as outsourced health government.

notes.title: 867 — Supplier-dependency review dockets: admin privileges, exit rehearsals, benefit claims, and no contract confidence by assertion
notes.thesis: A public body using cloud, SaaS, AI, identity, analytics, or managed-platform infrastructure should keep a supplier-dependency review docket that proves authority ownership, processor boundaries, privileged access, data and model location, product purpose, benefit claims, exit rehearsal, fallback continuity, redress, and opposition handling before procurement confidence, security assurance, or supplier reputation becomes a substitute for public governance.

notes.title: 868 — Municipal distress intervention and handback dockets: waivers, transition control, local capacity, and no democracy by permanent receivership
notes.thesis: A municipal fiscal-distress intervention should be treated as a temporary repair waist with a legal trigger, bounded powers, public-service continuity plan, democratic-damage ledger, fiscal-recovery evidence, local-capacity rebuild, waiver / reactivation clock, and dissolution or handback receipt, not as a permanent shadow government justified by past insolvency.

notes.title: 869 — Applied municipal handback case packet for Detroit Financial Review Commission: post-bankruptcy waiver, reactivation clock, and no local democracy by dormant receivership
notes.thesis: The Detroit Financial Review Commission case is best classified as a decreased-oversight municipal distress handback monitor: active state approval powers have been waived after repeated fiscal certifications, but the public-law form remains a live waiver / reactivation / eventual-release waist rather than either permanent receivership or ordinary local self-government with no residue.

notes.title: 870 — Symbolic authority and mandate-capacity mismatch dockets: formal bodies, real levers, transition receipts, and no accountability by mission statement
notes.thesis: A body becomes symbolically overloaded when it is publicly blamed, praised, funded, or reorganized as if it owns an outcome, while the legal powers, money, land, staff, data, contracts, operational discretion, and remedy routes needed to govern that outcome are split elsewhere; the archive should therefore test formal authority against operative levers before calling a body a government, a failure, a fix, or a thing ready to abolish.

notes.title: 871 — Applied symbolic-authority case packet for LAHSA: joint-powers homelessness waist, audit-triggered transition, city-county split, and no homelessness government by grant administrator
notes.thesis: The Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority is best classified as a mandate-capacity-mismatched homelessness coordination, data, and grant / contracting waist under transition: it is a real joint-powers authority with major funds, contracts, dashboards, and Continuum-of-Care duties, but it should not be treated as a general homelessness government because land, housing supply, health systems, local law, county programs, city programs, provider capacity, and appropriations sit across other principals.

notes.title: 872 — Capacity floor and fragile-jurisdiction implementation dockets: security, administration, donor dependence, records, and no authority by mandate print
notes.thesis: In fragile or low-capacity jurisdictions, the archive must not treat a mandate, compact, donor pledge, emergency authorization, stabilization plan, technical-assistance project, or international support mission as operative authority until the docket proves minimum implementability: security access, staffed operating lanes, money that actually arrives, records that can survive crisis, rights and accountability routes, and a handoff path back to ordinary local institutions.

notes.title: 873 — Applied fragile-jurisdiction case packet for Haiti Gang Suppression Force / UN Support Office / HNP: capacity floor and no security state by external logistics
notes.thesis: The honest form for Haiti's post-MSS security-support architecture is a fragile-jurisdiction international security-support and logistics waist around Haitian public responsibility: the Gang Suppression Force and UN Support Office may supply temporary capacity, protection, logistics, and pressure against armed groups, but they must not be read as a Haitian security state, a UN peacekeeping mission, a donor government, or proof of restored authority until access, staffing, funding, records, civilian-protection, accountability, and handback evidence exist.

notes.title: 874 — Model-mediated public decisions and evidentiary debt dockets: proof hierarchy, burden, notice, review, and no public debt by statistical proxy
notes.thesis: A model, data match, risk score, rule engine, calculator, or automated workflow may identify a question for public administration, but it must not become debt, benefit loss, sanction, custody, exclusion, enforcement, or other legal effect until the public authority can show a statute-specific evidence docket, lawful burden allocation, intelligible notice, meaningful review, and a public remedy route.

notes.title: 875 — Applied model-decision case packet for Robodebt: income averaging, welfare debts, appeal friction, and no social-security debt by automated proxy
notes.thesis: Robodebt should be classified as an unlawful evidentiary-proxy and automated debt-recovery public-law incident: a data-matching and income-averaging workflow turned discrepancy signals into social-security debts, shifted practical burden to recipients, exposed people to collection pressure, and now requires evidence, notice, review, legal-advice, remediation, and automated-decision guardrails before any successor system is trusted.

notes.title: 876 — Generative public-service assistants and guidance-liability dockets: source-bounded answers, reliance boundaries, and no law by chatbot
notes.thesis: A generative public-service assistant is a public guidance interface, not merely search and not a decision system by default; it needs a guidance-liability docket that proves source grounding, decision-boundary labels, freshness, evaluation, user reliance controls, incident correction, accessibility, safety, supplier / model-change records, and withdrawal or handoff routes before official-looking answers are trusted.

notes.title: 877 — Applied generative-assistant case packet for NYC MyCity Chatbot: business-guidance hallucination, beta withdrawal, and no municipal law by chatbot answer
notes.thesis: The NYC MyCity Chatbot should be classified as an official public guidance assistant whose beta status did not neutralize reliance risk: it was launched to give trusted business guidance, later audited for inaccurate and inconsistent answers, and now requires a withdrawal / transition receipt, incident ledger, corpus and evaluation record, and no municipal law by chatbot answer.

notes.title: 878 — Applied generative-assistant case packet for GOV.UK Chat: RAG guidance assistant, source links, limited pilot, and no benefit, tax, or visa decision by summary
notes.thesis: GOV.UK Chat should be classified as a source-bound public guidance assistant under staged expansion: its RAG design, algorithmic transparency record, source links, user warnings, evaluation, red-teaming, privacy controls, and app integration make it a stronger positive-control case than NYC MyCity, but its public-law safety still depends on keeping summaries below decision grade and preserving evaluation, corpus, model-change, incident, and escalation records.

notes.title: 879 — Staff-facing AI copilots, casework triage, draft records, and no public action by invisible autocomplete
notes.thesis: A staff-facing AI copilot is not safe merely because the public never sees it; when it drafts, summarizes, classifies, routes, prepopulates, flags, or records public-service work, it needs an internal action docket that proves use-case boundaries, source lineage, output capture, review quality, queue effects, sensitive-data controls, model-change records, and error feedback before invisible autocomplete becomes public action.

notes.title: 880 — Applied staff-copilot case packet for Redbox: general-purpose civil-service LLM, official-sensitive documents, use-case gates, and no policy by prompt
notes.thesis: Redbox is best classified as a general-purpose internal civil-service LLM copilot with diffuse use-case risk: it may be a safer sanctioned alternative to ad hoc public-model use, but official-sensitive security approval and productivity value do not prove decision-grade reliability, record completeness, or policy legitimacy.

notes.title: 881 — Applied staff-copilot case packet for DfE Correspondence Drafter: RAG, standard lines, human review, and no public reply by autocomplete
notes.thesis: DfE Correspondence Drafter is best classified as a staff-facing public-correspondence drafting waist: it may improve speed and consistency, but a human-review label is adequate only if the sent response, source pack, draft edits, quality assurance, issue reporting, and correction route remain visible.

notes.title: 882 — Applied staff-copilot case packet for ICO ICE 360 Case Creation Automation: LLM intake fields, contact matching, and no regulatory case by parser
notes.thesis: ICO ICE 360 Case Creation Automation is best classified as an intake-to-case-file automation waist: it does not decide outcomes or priority, but field creation, contact matching, data extraction, and queue readiness still need provenance, mismatch review, feedback loops, and source-image continuity because the case file starts where the parser writes.

notes.title: 883 — Applied staff-triage case packet for DWP Whitemail Insights and Vulnerability Scanner: letter classification, vulnerability shortlist, and no benefit decision by flag
notes.thesis: DWP Whitemail Insights and Vulnerability Scanner is best classified as a staff-facing triage and vulnerability-support waist: it does not decide benefit entitlement, but theme labels, vulnerability shortlists, urgent-support routing, false negatives, and human follow-up records still determine whether the state notices distress in time.

notes.title: 884 — Transition receipts and decommissioning dockets: rollback, replacement, migration, sunset, and no governance repair by disappearance
notes.thesis: A public tool, authority, platform, pilot, emergency measure, supplier arrangement, database, or coordination body is not repaired merely because it is paused, renamed, absorbed, replaced, made optional, or ended; the archive needs a transition receipt proving terminal status, successor function, affected-user notice, record preservation, data closeout, procurement / contract closeout, defect learning, and relaunch gates before disappearance becomes governance.

notes.title: 885 — Applied transition-receipt case packet for ArriveCAN: emergency border app, Advance Declaration conversion, procurement failures, and no modernization by survivorship
notes.thesis: ArriveCAN should be classified as an emergency digital border application converted into an optional Advance CBSA Declaration platform with serious management, procurement, testing, cost, and record failures in its emergency phase; the successor modernization use does not erase the emergency-period transition receipt, and there is no border modernization by survivorship.

notes.title: 886 — Applied transition-receipt case packet for NYC MyCity Chatbot beta closure: successor gates and no public AI repair by maintenance page
notes.thesis: The ended NYC MyCity Chatbot beta should be classified as a quiet public-AI withdrawal that still needs a transition receipt: a maintenance or beta-ended page can redirect users, but it cannot prove incident closure, affected-domain learning, source-corpus repair, successor gates, or no public AI repair by maintenance page.

notes.title: 887 — Platform migration and reprocurement dockets: parallel runs, data cutover, residual dependency, and no replacement by award notice
notes.thesis: A public platform has not been replaced, repaired, or safely migrated merely because a new supplier, product, portal, SaaS tenant, data hub, or digital proof channel has been selected; the archive needs a platform-migration docket proving old/new function mapping, data and identity continuity, backlog/error tail, interface dependencies, parallel-run reconciliation, cutover/rollback gates, user continuity, contract exit, legacy fallback, and post-migration value.

notes.title: 888 — Applied platform-migration case packet for Canada Phoenix-to-Dayforce payroll transition: backlog, parallel runs, data hub, and no pay repair by new SaaS
notes.thesis: Canada's Phoenix-to-Dayforce pay modernization should be classified as a high-risk payroll and HR platform migration under continuing affected-employee and public-owner duties; Dayforce feasibility and supplier selection are not pay repair until backlog residue, data migration, rule simplification, parallel runs, departmental readiness, compensation tails, and two-system operating risk are proven at cutover.

notes.title: 889 — Applied platform-migration case packet for UK eVisa / View and Prove digital-status migration: share codes, legacy documents, and no right by portal uptime
notes.thesis: The UK eVisa transition should be classified as a public-rights proof platform migration, not simply a digital convenience upgrade: the underlying immigration status may not change, but practical access to work, rent, benefits, travel, services, and third-party recognition can fail if account access, data correctness, legacy-document continuity, share-code systems, checker education, outage response, and assisted routes are not migration-gated.

notes.title: 890 — Ecological legal personhood and rights-of-nature implementation dockets: guardian spines, remedy budgets, monitoring, and no ecological repair by personhood declaration
notes.thesis: Recognizing a river, lagoon, forest, mountain, basin, wetland, glacier, reef, or other ecosystem as a legal person or rights-bearing subject is not ecological repair until the archive can see the guardian spine, public-owner boundary, affected-community authority, scientific baseline, remedy plan, money, enforcement path, monitoring record, liability boundary, and failure route.

notes.title: 891 — Applied ecological-personhood case packet for Colombia Atrato River: biocultural rights, guardian commission, illegal-mining plans, and no river governance by court declaration
notes.thesis: The Atrato River judgment is best classified as a biocultural-rights and ecological-personhood implementation waist: the river, basin, and tributaries were recognized as rights-bearing, but the governance proof lives in the guardian commission, community co-representation, anti-mining / decontamination plans, health and food-security duties, public records, and continuing capacity to turn a court declaration into ecological repair.

notes.title: 892 — Applied ecological-personhood case packet for Spain Mar Menor: legal-person lagoon, Tutoría, constitutional review, guardian committees, and no lagoon repair by tax number
notes.thesis: The Mar Menor arrangement is best classified as a statutory ecological legal-personhood and public-action waist: Law 19/2022 recognizes the lagoon and basin as a rights-bearing legal person, while the implementation proof lies in the Tutoría organs, scientific indicators, citizen and public representation, standing, administrative duties, contract / tax-number capacity, and whether ecological restoration follows rather than merely constitutional survival.

notes.title: 893 — Applied ecological-personhood negative control for Ganga / Yamuna: stayed juristic personhood, guardian liability, and no river repair by impracticable personhood
notes.thesis: The Ganga / Yamuna case is the archive's negative-control packet for ecological personhood: a court can recognize rivers as living legal persons and appoint state officials as guardians, yet the order may fail governance tests when jurisdiction, guardian liability, basin complexity, implementation capacity, and existing river-management duties are not made practicable.

notes.title: 894 — Entitlement continuity and procedural churn dockets: renewals, migration notices, ex parte proof, and no benefit loss by process failure
notes.thesis: When a person already holds health coverage, income support, housing support, disability-linked support, tax-credit support, immigration proof, or another public entitlement, the archive should not accept loss, closure, conversion, or migration as valid merely because a form, portal, notice, deadline, batch job, or system record says so; continuity requires a proof docket that separates legal eligibility, administrative status, notice reach, assistance, automatic renewal / transfer attempts, appeal and reinstatement routes, payment or service continuity, and actual remedy.

notes.title: 895 — Applied entitlement-continuity case packet for Medicaid / CHIP renewals: continuous-enrollment unwinding, ex parte renewals, procedural disenrollment, and no coverage loss by paperwork failure
notes.thesis: The Medicaid / CHIP unwinding should be classified as a mass entitlement-continuity and renewal-governance case: states had to resume eligibility renewals after continuous enrollment ended, but coverage loss is not cleanly legitimate unless records separate substantive ineligibility from procedural disenrollment, show serious ex parte renewal attempts, preserve notice and assistance routes, track pending / re-enrollment / transition outcomes, and retain federal / state accountability for process-caused coverage gaps.

notes.title: 896 — Applied entitlement-continuity case packet for UK Universal Credit managed migration: migration notices, transitional protection, legacy closures, and no income support by deadline letter
notes.thesis: Universal Credit managed migration should be classified as a deadline-triggered entitlement-continuity and benefit-conversion case: the migration notice is a lawful operating waist, but income-support continuity is not proven unless the record separates claim made, transitional protection awarded, not-claimed closure, in-progress cases, late claims, assisted support, vulnerability safeguards, appointee routes, and payment-gap remedies.

notes.title: 897 — Payment-entitlement, redress, and refund dockets: claimant proof, calculation, payment tail, dispute routes, and no repair by payable label
notes.thesis: When a public authority owes money because of a tax credit, refund, compensation scheme, redress programme, settlement implementation, wrongful conviction, administrative harm, support-scheme conversion, or emergency relief promise, the archive should not treat the debt as repaired merely because an amount is announced, a claim is registered, an offer is made, a cheque is issued, or a scheme is named; the authority must prove claimant identity, legal basis, calculation, evidence burden, payment receipt, interim-versus-final status, dispute route, fraud-control boundary, publication truth, and learning from the harm.

notes.title: 898 — Applied payment-redress case packet for Post Office Horizon: multipath redress schemes, family tail, legal costs, and no scandal repair by total paid
notes.thesis: The Post Office Horizon redress architecture is best classified as a multipath public redress and payment-state waist for institutional harm, wrongful convictions, shortfalls, litigation-group claimants, appeals, late applications, legal costs, family harm, and scheme closure; it should not be scored as repaired merely because total redress paid is high or one scheme reports near-completion.

notes.title: 899 — Applied payment-redress case packet for the Infected Blood Compensation Authority: core and adjusted routes, support-scheme transition, community feedback, and no redress by offer count
notes.thesis: The Infected Blood Compensation Authority is best classified as a statutory compensation and support-transition authority for infected, affected, deceased-person, and support-scheme-linked claimants; it should not be scored as redress by offer count, tariff existence, or headline paid total until route choice, support-scheme continuity, estate and affected-person access, community-feedback response, reassessment, and payment-state tails are visible.

notes.title: 900 — Applied payment-refund case packet for IRS Employee Retention Credit: backlog, fraud screening, disallowance clock, and no tax relief by claim form or indefinite review
notes.thesis: The Employee Retention Credit refund tail is best classified as a fraud-screened refundable-tax-credit payment waist with eligibility proof, amended-return processing, promoter-risk controls, claim inventory, disallowance notices, refund-suit limitation clocks, and communication duties; it should not be scored as relief merely because a claim was filed, nor as program integrity merely because payment was delayed or disallowed.

notes.title: 901 — Identity credential access and delegated authority dockets: assurance levels, recovery, relying-party boundaries, and no public service by login
notes.thesis: Public digital identity is an access waist, not the right itself: a login, proofing score, assurance level, passkey, biometric check, wallet credential, or delegated mandate must be treated as evidence for a bounded service action, not as entitlement, eligibility, consent, agency, or lawful denial.

notes.title: 902 — Applied credential-access case packet for Login.gov IAL2 assurance repair: federal identity provider, standards reliance, and no trust by assertion
notes.thesis: Login.gov should be classified as a federal shared identity-provider and assurance-repair waist: useful because it can centralize sign-in, proofing, in-person routes, fraud controls, and federation, but high-risk because relying agencies can over-credit assurance claims unless standard version, service offering, certification scope, billing, fallback, and user exclusion records stay public.

notes.title: 903 — Applied credential-access case packet for IRS Online Account / ID.me: tax records, payments, authorizations, and no tax right by private credential
notes.thesis: IRS Online Account and ID.me should be classified as a private-provider credential-access waist for tax records, payments, notices, authorizations, and selected forms: a useful fraud and privacy control, but not the tax right itself, and not a lawful basis to deny transcripts, payment control, refund information, representative authorization, or deadline protection when proofing, device, account, or biometric routes fail.

notes.title: 904 — Applied credential-access case packet for GOV.UK One Login: central-government front door, identity proofing, incidents, and no service by single sign-on
notes.thesis: GOV.UK One Login should be classified as a central-government credential-access and federation waist: promising because it can reduce duplicative sign-in and proofing methods, but high-stakes because a single front door, OpenID Connect integration, identity proofing, account recovery, digital documents, service onboarding, and status-page incidents can become practical access control for many distinct services.

notes.title: 905 — Representative access, proxy authority, and fiduciary dockets: scope, consent, revocation, payment control, and no public action by password sharing
notes.thesis: When someone acts for another person before the state, the archive must not treat a login, family relationship, professional role, payment account, appointeeship, power of attorney, guardian order, representative payee appointment, tax authorization, or appeal form as interchangeable authority; every representative route needs a scoped mandate, capacity or consent basis, revocation path, notice and record trail, payment / information boundary, and direct-rights fallback for the person represented.

notes.title: 906 — Applied representative-access case packet for Social Security representative payee: benefit management, misuse, restitution, and no welfare by informal fiduciary
notes.thesis: The Social Security representative payee programme should be classified as a payment-fiduciary representative-access waist: SSA appoints a person or organization to receive and manage Social Security or SSI payments for a beneficiary who cannot manage them, but the appointment does not transfer ownership of the funds, erase beneficiary voice, authorize non-SSA financial control, or prove welfare delivery merely because money reached the payee.

notes.title: 907 — Applied representative-access case packet for UK benefit appointees and third-party representatives: capacity, wishes, migration, and no support by account holder alone
notes.thesis: UK benefit appointeeship and third-party representative routes should be classified as a benefit-claim and payment-management representative-access waist: an appointee may make and maintain claims and manage payments for someone who cannot do so, while a third-party representative may support a person who can decide; neither route should become mere account-holder control, password sharing, or transfer of all welfare authority by administrative convenience.

notes.title: 908 — Applied representative-access case packet for IRS Tax Pro Account / CAF / POA / TIA authorizations: scope, revocation, and no tax practice by checkbox
notes.thesis: IRS Tax Pro Account, Centralized Authorization File records, Power of Attorney, and Tax Information Authorization should be classified as a professional and third-party representative-access waist: digital authorization can speed tax representation and disclosure, but a checkbox, online-account approval, CAF entry, or tax-professional credential cannot replace matter scope, period limits, professional eligibility, taxpayer consent, revocation, notice routing, and non-digital alternatives.

notes.title: 909 — Applied representative-access case packet for Marketplace and Medicare appeal representation: scope, health information, notices, and no appeal right by form friction
notes.thesis: Marketplace and Medicare appeal representation should be classified as a health-coverage representative-access waist: a person may appoint someone to act in an appeal, claim, grievance, or request, but representation must preserve scope, health-information authorization, notice routing, expiry, revocation, legal-representative alternatives, expedited health-risk access, and the underlying appeal right despite form friction.

notes.title: 910 — Cloudtainer maintenance, source health, gap ledgers, generated-surface budgets, and no datacube by self-consistency
notes.thesis: A datacube that passes its own lint is only self-consistent; the next maintenance layer must track source health, external freshness, missing-case gaps, generated-surface budgets, package hygiene, and deletion or merge queues before it adds more case prose.

notes.title: 911 — Disaster-assistance survivor proof, program fragmentation, appeals, recovery-delivery dockets, and no relief by denial letter
notes.thesis: Disaster assistance is not governed by declaring a disaster, opening a portal, or issuing status letters; it needs a survivor-proof docket that separates eligibility, identity, occupancy, ownership, damage, insurance, duplication of benefits, program handoffs, appeals, payments, and recovery outcomes.

notes.title: 912 — Applied disaster-assistance case packet for FEMA Individual Assistance, identity, ownership, occupancy, damage, appeals, SBA sequence, and no recovery by status letter
notes.thesis: FEMA Individual Assistance is a disaster-survivor recovery-delivery waist: it must separate registration, identity, occupancy, ownership, disaster-caused need, insurance, duplication, inspection, appeals, payment, and handoff state before a status letter is treated as recovery or denial.

notes.title: 913 — Unemployment insurance integrity, claimant access, identity, payment hold, overpayment, waiver, and no benefit by fraud flag
notes.thesis: Unemployment-insurance integrity is not one control problem: eligibility, separation, identity, certification, payment release, fraud suspicion, overpayment, waiver, appeal, recovery, and claimant access are separate states, and no benefit should disappear by fraud flag alone.

notes.title: 914 — Applied unemployment-insurance case packet for pandemic UI, PUA, identity proofing, payment holds, overpayments, waivers, appeals, and no integrity by payment block
notes.thesis: Pandemic UI and PUA form a federal-state benefit-integrity and claimant-access waist: identity proofing, eligibility, fraud flags, payment holds, overpayments, waivers, appeals, recovery, and modernization must be separated before blocked payment is treated as integrity or paid benefit as success.

notes.title: 915 — Watchlist, border, law-enforcement automation, biometric screening, redress, and no enforcement by match
notes.thesis: Watchlist, border, and law-enforcement automation must split nomination, dissemination, screening hit, biometric candidate, officer confirmation, action, redress, deletion, and downstream correction; no enforcement action should be treated as justified by a match alone.

notes.title: 916 — Applied watchlist and border automation case packet for U.S. terrorist screening, DHS TRIP, CBP biometrics, NCIC encounters, and no liberty by alert
notes.thesis: The U.S. terrorist-screening, border-biometric, DHS TRIP, and nonfederal NCIC encounter ecosystem is a security-screening and redress-propagation waist: it may support protection and identity verification, but no liberty, travel, border, or police consequence should be justified by alert alone.

notes.title: 917 — Public AI register maintenance, inventory drift, risk state, and no governance by listing
notes.thesis: A public AI inventory, algorithmic-transparency register, or high-risk-system database is a truth-maintenance waist, not an authorization instrument: listing, absence, stale status, or machine-readable neatness should never by itself prove lawful, safe, deployed, retired, or governed use.

notes.title: 918 — Applied public AI register case packet for federal AI use-case inventories, SBA, IRS, ATRS, EU database, and no use by inventory row
notes.thesis: The U.S. federal AI use-case inventory, late SBA reporting, IRS public/internal inventory split, UK ATRS, and EU high-risk AI database together form a public AI register maintenance case: transparency rows must be reconciled to live use, risk, monitoring, redress, and retirement evidence, with no public use by inventory row.

notes.title: 919 — Subnational digital government and local AI implementation, procurement, benefits, schools, courts, policing, permitting, and no accountability by local pilot
notes.thesis: State, provincial, municipal, school, court, police, and local-service AI must be governed at the implementation seam where procurement, public records, local authority, staff practice, affected-person routes, and service consequences meet; a local pilot, policy template, or inventory row is never enough to prove accountability.

notes.title: 920 — Applied subnational AI case packet for NYC algorithmic tools, California ADS inventory, Colorado AI Act, courts, schools, local records, and no public service by local pilot
notes.thesis: NYC’s algorithmic-tool reporting, California’s high-risk ADS inventory, Colorado’s AI Act, state-court AI guidance, school AI guidance, and local-government public-records practice form a subnational implementation packet: inventories, laws, pilots, policies, and records only count when they trace to a concrete public-service workflow and correction route.

notes.title: 921 — Non-English / Global South official-source governance, language-version drift, translation currentness, and no rule by English summary
notes.thesis: Non-English and Global South official sources must be governed as live authority, service, language, and currentness objects; an English summary, machine translation, donor deck, benchmark paragraph, or central-government press release is never enough to prove the rule, service route, remedy, or affected-person burden.

notes.title: 922 — Applied non-English / Global South source case packet for Brazil CadÚnico, gov.br, Bolsa Família, AI plan, LGPD, India Aadhaar, DigiLocker, and no benefit by translated summary
notes.thesis: Brazil’s CadÚnico / gov.br / Bolsa Família / AI-and-data-governance stack, with India’s Aadhaar and DigiLocker as a comparator, is a source-language and public-service delivery packet: digital identity, data integration, AI strategy, benefit qualification, and official multilingual surfaces only count when authoritative-language sources connect to cure, appeal, assistance, and payment evidence.

notes.title: 923 — Health-benefit and prescription-drug coverage-transition dockets, payer handoff, formulary clocks, prior authorization, and no treatment continuity by enrollment row
notes.thesis: Health-coverage and prescription-drug transitions are not safe because an enrollment row, plan card, formulary row, renewal status, special-enrollment period, or payment option exists; continuity requires a treatment-level docket that proves payer handoff, medication access, utilization-management cure, cost-sharing feasibility, notice reach, assisted navigation, and appeal / retroactive repair before a person experiences a gap.

notes.title: 924 — Applied health-coverage and prescription transition case packet for Medicaid / CHIP, Marketplace, and Medicare Part D renewals, SEPs, formulary exceptions, and no medication continuity by plan card
notes.thesis: The U.S. Medicaid / CHIP unwinding, Marketplace transfer, and Medicare Part D transition-fill / exception / payment-plan stack shows why health-benefit governance must track treatment-level continuity: a person can move across coverage statuses and still lose medication, cost protection, prescriber support, or appeal time.

notes.title: 925 — Utility shutoff, medical baseline, and climate-continuity dockets: arrears, outage, cooling, electricity-dependent equipment, and no life safety by account code
notes.thesis: A utility account flag, medical-baseline certificate, LIHEAP award, outage map, arrears plan, cooling-center list, or reconnect promise does not prove life-safety continuity; the governing object is the joined docket across account state, health risk, climate hazard, assistance posting, communications, backup power, reconnection, and aftercare.

notes.title: 926 — Applied utility-shutoff and medical-baseline case packet for EIA disconnection data, LIHEAP, HHS emPOWER, Connecticut winter protection, California PSPS, and no safety by medical certificate
notes.thesis: The U.S. utility-shutoff / medical-baseline case proves why billing protection, energy assistance, medical certification, outage notification, and public-health mapping must be joined: no household is safe merely because a utility record, benefit award, map, or certificate says so.

notes.title: 927 — Cloudtainer deep-read audit: schema drift, source-health coverage, generated-surface budgets, housing gap, and no maintenance by green lint
notes.thesis: Rev0745 is substantively coherent, but a green lint result still hid schema identity drift, status-vocabulary drift, weak generated-surface budgets, uneven source-currentness coverage, and an under-sourced housing gap; the repair rule is **no maintenance by green lint**.

notes.title: 928 — Housing stability, eviction, rental assistance, tenant screening, and possession-continuity dockets: no housing stability by portal status
notes.thesis: A rental-assistance application, portal approval, eviction filing, court representation flag, tenant-screening report, shelter referral, or landlord ledger does not prove housing stability; the governing object is the joined docket across household, unit, arrears, assistance posting, possession, court, representation, screening record, shelter / relocation, and aftercare state.

notes.title: 929 — Applied housing-continuity case packet for Eviction Lab, ERA closeout, CFPB tenant screening, NYC Right to Counsel, Illinois CBRAP, and no stability by portal status
notes.thesis: The current U.S. housing-continuity case shows why eviction filings, rental-assistance closeout, tenant-screening enforcement, right-to-counsel implementation, court-based rental assistance, and homelessness counts must be joined: no household is stable merely because a portal, docket, program page, report, or screening record says so.

notes.title: 930 — Cyber incident, software provenance, and public-service continuity dockets: runtime SBOM, supplier access, recovery, and no resilience by attestation
notes.thesis: A secure-software attestation, SBOM, inventory row, CPG checklist, breach notice, incident page, uptime statement, or restoration announcement is not public-service resilience. Cyber/software continuity needs a joined docket across public function, supplier, runtime asset, privileged access, exploitable exposure, degraded operation, data exposure, notification, recovery, and affected-person tail.

notes.title: 931 — Applied cyber/software-continuity case packet for Change Healthcare, Synnovis, British Library, OMB/NIST/CISA, and no resilience by attestation
notes.thesis: Change Healthcare, Synnovis, the British Library, and federal secure-software assurance reforms show the same administrative failure mode: a cyber event is not just a breach, outage, or compliance control problem. It is a supplier-dependent public-service continuity event unless claims, appointments, payments, access, records, data rights, degraded mode, recovery, and affected-person repair are joined.

notes.title: 932 — Election administration continuity dockets: registration, ballot mail, accessibility, canvass, audit, certification, and no suffrage by status row
notes.thesis: An election is not proven by a registration row, polling-place lookup, mailpiece scan, accessible-machine checkbox, unofficial result, audit slogan, or certified total. notes.title: 956 — Tax filing, refund, credit, ITIN, offset, identity-theft, and free-file continuity dockets: no tax relief by return row

notes.thesis: Consumer financial access is not a bank-account row, credit-report row, score, validation notice, complaint submission, error-resolution ticket, prepaid-card registration, overdraft disclosure, or regulator referral. notes.thesis: CFPB complaint data, FDIC household-banking categories, credit-report tools, FCRA/Regulation V disputes, debt-collection validation notices, Regulation E/prepaid error-resolution rules, OCC complaint routing, and bank-account consumer tools are separate evidence lanes. notes.title: 960 — Cloudtainer release-lineage, schema-gap, generated-surface, and maintenance-revision audit: no maintenance by green lint
notes.thesis: Rev0762 is substantively useful, but the cloudtainer had three false-green maintenance risks: `rev0761` existed in archive metadata while disappearing from the release index, `metadata/gap_ledger.json` violated its own schema for one repaired gap while lint passed, and maintenance-only revisions were again pressured toward fake operational matrix coverage; the repair rule is **no maintenance by green lint**.

The continuity test has to follow whether the person can open, keep, fund, withdraw from, and repair a transaction account or wallet after screening-file denials, fraud/KYC holds, unexpected closures, garnishment orders, custodial-ledger breaks, and bank/fintech partner failures.

notes.title: 962 — Applied deposit-account access case packet for ChexSystems, Early Warning, Reg CC, garnishment, closed-account reopening, Synapse, custodial ledgers, and no usable money by account approval
notes.thesis: A deposit account, prepaid card, fintech wallet, or app balance proves usable money only when the packet joins screening, account state, funds availability, protected-payment, custodial-ledger, complaint, and household-outcome evidence.

notes.title: 963 — Cloudtainer mission deep-read, stale front door, generated source surface, and source-health backlog: no mission by route mass
notes.thesis: The archive's heart is an evidence-continuity discipline for public power: a status row, register entry, approval, portal, dashboard, app balance, or generated route is never the same thing as a person-level outcome, working remedy, or maintained source posture. Rev0764 is strong on usable-money continuity, but the cloudtainer still showed a false-green front-door break, a wasteful generated source reader, and a source-health backlog; the repair rule is **no mission by route mass**.

notes.title: 964 — Cloudtainer risk triage, thread-route compaction, source-health backfill, and no forward motion by new docket
notes.thesis: The riskiest unfinished work is not another broad domain packet; it is the archive's operating spine: unchecked high-dependency sources, megabyte-scale thread/source-health surfaces, and weak pressure to turn maintenance debt into smaller reader routes. This revision moves substance by checking the top source-health queue, compacting the thread and source-health machine surfaces, and adopting **no forward motion by new docket**.

notes.title: 965 — Cloudtainer source-index compaction, priority source-health second tranche, and no completion by unresolved warning
notes.thesis: Forward motion in this cloudtainer means closing the warning that is already visible, backfilling the sources that carry the most public-consequence dependency, and refusing to count another registry or docket as completion while generated surfaces and unchecked live sources still carry the risk.

notes.title: 966 — Cloudtainer test-surface budget, priority source-health third tranche, and no substance by matrix sprawl
notes.thesis: The next risk was not a missing doctrine family; it was a maintenance accounting error that treated every test-matrix leaf render as front-door sprawl, plus a large block of high-dependency source keys still lacking health posture. This revision separates reader-route pressure from evidence-library coverage, then uses the freed maintenance lane to review the next high-consequence source tranche.

notes.title: 967 — Cloudtainer source-health closure, catalog triage, retirement queue, and no completion by catalog posture
notes.thesis: The riskiest unfinished work was no longer a giant generated file or a missing docket. It was the remaining class of source keys that still had no explicit posture, plus a retirement audit that named many possible overlaps but did not create a small actionable merge queue. This revision closes the unclassified source-health backlog while separating direct review from catalog triage, then adds a bounded merge-packet queue so maintenance can reduce route mass without pretending that overlap equals deletion readiness.

notes.title: 968 — Cloudtainer direct-refresh tranche, first merge packet, and no route retirement by similarity score
notes.thesis: The riskiest unfinished work after rev0769 was not another policy domain. It was the gap between catalog-triaged source posture and actual direct refresh, plus a retirement queue that could still tempt maintainers to treat lexical overlap as safe deletion. This revision refreshes the highest-consequence catalog rows and turns the top retirement candidate into a preservation packet rather than a deletion shortcut.

notes.title: 969 — Cloudtainer direct-refresh tranche, second merge packet, and no completion by refresh percentage
notes.thesis: The archive has now moved past the easiest repair traps: generated surfaces are compact, all source keys have a posture, and route overlap has a packet queue. The riskiest remaining failure is subtler: treating a higher direct-review percentage as completion while the remaining unrefreshed rows are exactly the kinds of live, rights-bearing, or remedy-bearing surfaces that can change underneath a polished catalog.

notes.title: 970 — Cloudtainer direct-refresh tranche, absorption guard, and no route absorption by preservation gesture
notes.thesis: The riskiest remaining work is now concentrated in two places: live or consequence-bearing source rows that still depend on catalog posture, and route-retirement candidates that can be reviewed forever without ever producing an absorption-ready successor. This revision keeps direct-refresh work moving while adding a stronger merge-packet guard: a preservation packet must say what a future absorption patch would have to preserve, not merely why deletion is unsafe.

notes.title: 971 — Cloudtainer catalog queue closure, follow-up capture, service-home absorption patch, and no reliance by direct-review percent
notes.thesis: Closing a catalog-only source queue is maintenance progress, not reliance readiness: a source can be directly refreshed and still require blocked-route, PDF, sparse-page, or search-index follow-up before it can carry quote-level, legal, or outcome-continuity authority.

notes.title: 972 — Cloudtainer follow-up capture trim, source-health clock split, and no clean source by review clock

notes.title: 973 — Cloudtainer capture queue closure, service-home test parity, and no reliance by clean-source count

notes.thesis: The archive now knows which UI claimant and housing household tails it needs, but the riskiest next failure is calling that plan field validation; rev0790 turns the plans into sampling, nonresponse-bias, privacy, and source-preservation gates while keeping them non-closing.

notes.title: 989 — Cloudtainer field-intake controls, consent/linkage firewalls, source-preservation safeguards, and no fieldwork by gate
notes.thesis: Rev0790 made sampling gates concrete, but a sampling gate can still become dangerous theater if it is treated as permission to contact people, link administrative records, or store private lives; rev0791 adds field-intake controls so claimant and household evidence cannot move forward without lawful-basis, consent/waiver, PII-separation, linkage-key, adverse-action, and publication firewalls.

notes.title: 990 — Cloudtainer fieldwork authorization gates, data-custody handoffs, oversight receipts, and no collection by control
notes.thesis: Rev0791 made field-intake controls safe enough to name a possible UI or housing tail, but intake controls still do not name who may authorize contact, who may hold linkage keys, where private records may live, or when outputs may leave a secure environment; rev0792 adds fieldwork authorization gates so collection cannot begin merely because the cube has a design, consent floor, or control checklist.

notes.title: 991 — Cloudtainer fieldwork execution controls, incident clocks, audit logs, retention/release, and no outcome by operating log
notes.thesis: Rev0792 established that fieldwork cannot begin from a design control, consent checklist, or authorization packet alone; rev0793 adds the missing execution layer so even authorized UI or housing fieldwork would need pause clocks, incident reporting, audit-log review, breach response, retention/disposition authority, and disclosure-reviewed release before any result can be trusted.

notes.title: 992 — Cloudtainer fieldwork release controls, disclosure limitation, public-output audit, and no outcome by release packet
notes.thesis: Rev0793 made fieldwork execution safe enough to describe without collecting anything. Rev0794 adds the missing release layer: even after future lawful approval, collection, incident handling, audit review, and retention checks, no public output may be treated as claimant or household outcome proof unless disclosure limitation, de-identification limits, method integrity, harm review, and errata/retraction controls have passed outside the cube.

notes.title: 993 — Cloudtainer fieldwork correction controls, errata/withdrawal/redress ledgers, and no outcome by corrigendum
notes.thesis: Rev0794 made public release safer to describe without releasing anything. Rev0795 adds the missing post-release layer: if a future public output is later found wrong, harmful, misleading, disclosure-risky, denominator-defective, or source-stale, the cube must know how to correct, withdraw, notify, version, and preserve the correction trail without treating the correction packet as the lived outcome.

notes.title: 994 — Cloudtainer redress verification controls, follow-through ledgers, internal-control repair, and no outcome by redress route
notes.thesis: Rev0795 made post-release correction safer to describe without correcting anything. Rev0796 adds the missing follow-through layer: even after a future correction, withdrawal, redress route, or notification, the cube must require separate verification that affected claimants or households were actually made whole.

notes.title: 995 — Cloudtainer closure dossiers, attestation matrix, gap reopen triggers, and no outcome by attestation
notes.thesis: Rev0796 made redress-verification follow-through explicit, but a verified redress control can still become another theater surface. Rev0797 adds non-private closure-dossier controls so the cube can say exactly what would be needed before any future gap closure while preserving unresolved exceptions, reopening triggers, and the rule that attestation is not the outcome.

notes.title: 996 — Cloudtainer post-closure monitoring, reopen clocks, drift guards, and no closure forever
notes.thesis: Rev0797 made closure dossiers reviewable but still non-ready. Rev0798 adds post-closure monitoring controls so any future closure remains conditional: recurrence, source decay, denominator drift, policy change, private-data leakage, or later claimant/household evidence can qualify or reopen a gap. The governing rule is **no closure forever**.

notes.title: 997 — Stewardship no custody
notes.thesis: A ZIP is not a custodian.
